items.item_text: Bachelor's degree in related area and/or equivalent experience/training.
BA in accounting or finance (Analyst III Supervisor); MBA, CPA, (Analyst IV-Supervisor) or other advanced education or certification in accounting or finances.
6 - 10 years of related experience.
Previous supervisory/managerial experience.
Participates in the creation, maintenance and reporting of operational and budget processes, academic and/or staff FTE, finance, human resources and space planning. (20% time)
Supervises the work of a department with responsibility for quality and quantity of work. (20% time)

Department expert for the management of all extramural activity. Supervise Contract and Grant Analysts as they prepare monthly financial statements for faculty and submit proposals using various web-based systems such as Cayuse424, NSF Fastlane, Research.Gov, and UCR's Electronic Campus Approval Form (eCAF). Reallocate responsibilities as workload changes occur, maintaining a balanced and fair distribution of responsibilities and effort. Serves as back-up support for Analysts during heavy proposal deadlines and/or staff shortages. (20% time)

Prepare monthly, annual, and ad hoc financial reports of departmental operations that incorporate history, current picture, and trends to support senior level decision making. Reconcile financial reports to the financial system ledgers; ensure that all financial transactions are reviewed promptly and that all required correcting entries are well explained, approved, appropriately documented, and posted in a timely manner. Manage financial operations so that only minimal correcting entries are necessary. Remain current on emerging information technologies, particularly as they relate to departmental financial, purchasing, and travel operations. Attend financial system user group meetings, college administrators meetings, college financial managers' meetings, Contract & Grant User group meetings, etc. Disseminate relevant information to those not in attendance. Responsible for fiscal year end closing. (15% time)
Participates in the development and monitoring of policies and procedures for departmental operations. (10% time)
Selects, develops, and evaluates personnel to ensure the effective and efficient operation of the function. (10% time)
May manage systems and procedures to protect departmental assets. (5% time)
Read/Comprehend: Constantly
Write: Constantly
Perform Calculations: Constantly
Communicate Orally: Constantly
Reason & Analyze: Constantly
Sit: Constantly
Stand: Occasionally
Walk: Occasionally

Solid knowledge of the organization's processes, protocols and procedures with a focus on budget, account and fund management and/or personnel management within labor contract(s) and personnel policy.

Experience in an academic environment providing support for staff and/or faculty knowledge of current University policies and procedures and a working knowledge of laws, regulations, policies, and procedures which apply to this position.
Solid knowledge of financial analysis and reporting techniques; human resources and risk management planning; accounting and payroll.
Demonstrated skills in employee supervision and HR administration.
Solid knowledge of common organization-specific and other computer application programs.
Solid organizational and customer service skills to effectively manage multiple priorities.
Solid interpersonal skills including verbal and written communication, active listening, critical thinking, persuasiveness, advising, and counseling to effectively motivate others.
Solid skills to quickly evaluate complex issues and identify resolution.
Experience preparing grant proposal and/or operational budgets
Interpersonal skills to effectively motivate others.
Demonstrated experience with pre-and post-award phases of contract & grant administration.
